title: Annapurna Circuit Trek: Full Guide
excerpt: The complete guide to the Annapurna Circuit trek: the route day by day, Tilicho Lake, the Thorong La pass, acclimatization, permits, seasons and cost.
seoTitle: Annapurna Circuit Trek Guide: Route, Thorong La, Cost and Season

content.value: On day 13 of the trek, before first light, trekkers leave Thorong High Camp at 4,880 m and start climbing in the dark toward the Thorong La pass, 5,416 m (17,769 ft), the highest point of the Annapurna Circuit. The Annapurna Circuit trek is a walking loop around the Annapurna range in north-central Nepal: it climbs the Marsyangdi river valley, crosses the pass and descends to Muktinath on the other side. It requires no climbing experience, but it does require good fitness, about two weeks in Nepal and patience with the acclimatization process. The recommended seasons are spring and fall, before and after the monsoon.

The Annapurna Circuit is one of the classic treks of the Himalaya. In nine days of walking it leads from a green valley of waterfalls and forests to a dry high-mountain landscape, past stone-built villages, Buddhist temples and prayer flags. This guide is based on the trek we run, the 16-day Annapurna Circuit, which adds Tilicho Lake, 4,919 m, to the classic route. It answers the questions people ask before signing up: how the route is built, why altitude sets the pace, what awaits on the pass, when to go and what it costs.
What the Annapurna Circuit is

The Annapurna range rises in north-central Nepal, and its highest summit, Annapurna I, reaches 8,091 m. The circuit goes around the range: it starts in the Marsyangdi river valley, climbs to Manang, the main village of the upper valley, crosses the Thorong La pass and descends to Muktinath, on the edge of the Mustang region. Almost the whole route lies within the Annapurna Conservation Area.

The usual direction, which we follow too, is east to west: from the Marsyangdi valley and Manang to the pass, and from there to Muktinath. In this direction the ascent is gradual and there is time to acclimatize. In the opposite direction you have to climb more than 1,600 m in a single day from Muktinath to the pass, which is a much harder and riskier day.

Over the years dirt roads have been built along large parts of the route, on both sides of the pass, so most organized treks start walking higher up the valley and finish by vehicle. We drive by jeep from Kathmandu to Chame, 2,670 m, and continue on foot from there. Driving higher, as far as Manang, saves days, but it raises the risk of altitude sickness, because the body reaches high altitude without a gradual ascent.

Along the way the scenery and the culture change. In the lower part you walk beside the river, between waterfalls and forests, and in the upper part Buddhist villages, old temples, prayer wheels and colorful prayer flags appear. To the south rise Annapurna II and Gangapurna, and to the northeast Pisang Peak.

content.value: Our route, day by day
This is how HighAir's Annapurna Circuit trek is built. The altitudes in brackets are those of the overnight stop or of the high point of that day:

items: Day 1: arrival in Kathmandu and transfer to the hotel.
Day 2: preparation day in Kathmandu, a briefing with the local guides and a gear check.
Day 3: a 6 to 7 hour jeep drive from Kathmandu to Besisahar (760 m), along the Trishuli river.
Day 4: a jeep drive along the Marsyangdi river, through the village of Tal, to Chame (2,670 m).
Day 5: the first walking day, from Chame to Pisang (3,200 m), with Annapurna II to the south.
Day 6: from Pisang to Manang (3,540 m), past old Buddhist temples.
Day 7: acclimatization day in Manang, with short walks around the village.
Day 8: from Manang to Shri Kharka (4,080 m).
Day 9: from Shri Kharka to Tilicho Base Camp (4,150 m).
Day 10: early climb to Tilicho Lake (4,919 m) and back to sleep at Tilicho Base Camp.
Day 11: back to the main circuit trail, to Leddar (4,200 m).
Day 12: from Leddar to Thorong High Camp (4,880 m).
Day 13: crossing the Thorong La pass (5,416 m) and down to Muktinath (3,800 m).
Day 14: a 7 to 8 hour jeep drive from Muktinath to Pokhara (820 m).
Day 15: flight from Pokhara to Kathmandu and a free day in the city.
Day 16: transfer to the airport and flight home.

content.value: The trek has nine days on the trail, from Chame to Muktinath. Walking days last between 4 and 10 hours, and distances range from 7 to 17 km a day. The pass day is the most demanding of all: 16 to 17 km, 9 to 10 hours of walking, and the highest point of the trek. The large bag, up to 15 kg per person, is carried by the porters, and you walk with a daypack only. Throughout the trek you sleep in teahouses, in twin rooms, and eat three meals a day chosen from the teahouse menu.

content.title: ✦ Seven nights between Manang and the pass
content.value: The common recommendation is to sleep at least five nights between arriving in Manang and crossing the Thorong La. Our itinerary has seven: two nights in Manang, a night at Shri Kharka, two nights at Tilicho Base Camp, a night at Leddar and a night at Thorong High Camp.
The way to Tilicho Lake

Tilicho Lake, at 4,919 m, is one of the highest lakes in the world. It lies west of Manang, below Tilicho Peak, and the way to it is a side branch of the main circuit trail. In our itinerary it takes four days: from Manang to Shri Kharka and Tilicho Base Camp, a climb to the lake and back, and then a crossing to Leddar on the main trail.

Beyond the scenery, Tilicho has a role in acclimatization. On day 10 you climb from Tilicho Base Camp to the lake, 769 m above where you slept, and return to sleep at base camp. This is the principle of "climb high, sleep low": the body meets an altitude of 4,919 m three days before the Thorong La, and comes back down to recover. This walking day lasts 7 to 8 hours, 11 to 12 km, and you set out for it early in the morning.

content.value: Acclimatization: why altitude sets the pace

The main risk on the Annapurna Circuit is not technical but physiological. The higher you go, the less oxygen each breath brings in, and the body needs time to adapt. Altitude sickness usually starts with a headache, sometimes joined by loss of appetite, dizziness, fatigue and nausea. When symptoms get worse despite rest at the same altitude, you descend.

Our itinerary is built around this principle. Walking starts at Chame, 2,670 m, and no higher. In Manang, 3,540 m, there is a full acclimatization day with short walks in the area. After Shri Kharka come two days on which the sleeping altitude barely changes, to Tilicho Base Camp and to Leddar, and between them the climb to Tilicho Lake, where you climb high and come back to sleep low. Only after all of that do you go up to Thorong High Camp.

Every group carries a pulse oximeter and a satellite device, and during the trek families at home receive WhatsApp updates. Our rule is simple: safety before the summit. In the mountains there is no promise of reaching the goal, but there is always a commitment to safety above all.
The Thorong La pass

The Thorong La, 5,416 m, is one of the highest mountain passes in the world crossed on foot, and it links the Manang valley in the east with Muktinath in the west. It cannot be crossed from Manang in a single day, so you sleep before it at Thorong High Camp, 4,880 m, the highest overnight stop of the trek.

You set out in the dark, before first light. The reason is the wind: on the pass it usually strengthens a few hours after sunrise, and it is best to be over the top and on the way down before then. The climb from High Camp to the pass is long and slow, in severe cold, so full warm clothing, gloves and a face cover are part of the essential gear. When there is snow or ice on the trail, mainly in spring, it becomes slippery, and trekkers usually use light crampons. The weather on the pass can delay the crossing, and the decision on when to cross belongs to the guides on the ground.

From the pass a wide view opens over the Annapurna range, Dhaulagiri, 8,167 m, and the mountains of Mustang. Then begins a descent of 1,616 m to Muktinath, 3,800 m. The descent is steep and long and hard on the knees, so healthy knees and trekking poles make a big difference. Muktinath is home to the Muktinath temple, a pilgrimage site sacred to Hindus and Buddhists, which you can visit at the end of the pass day.

content.value: Difficulty, and who the trek suits

We grade the Annapurna Circuit as a trek of moderate difficulty, and no climbing experience is required. What it takes is endurance: days of 4 to 10 hours of walking with a daypack, day after day, at an altitude that rises gradually to above 4,000 m. The main difficulty is the pass day, which requires a start in the dark, a long ascent and a long descent.

Previous trekking experience is not a requirement. If you can walk about 20 km a day, enjoy a challenge and come with strong motivation, the trek can suit you. The best preparation is long hikes with a pack, up and down hills, in the months before departure. A medical certificate and health declaration are required from every participant, and anyone who does not meet the health or physical requirements will not be able to join.

Before departure you receive a personal gear checklist and an online gear consultation, and the group meets the guide on an online preparation call. That way you reach Nepal with the right gear, already knowing the people you will walk with.

Good to know: the trek is led by professional local guides from Nepal who speak English and have long experience leading groups in the mountains. Basic English, enough to follow instructions on the trail, is worth having. Following the instructions of the crew is mandatory, and the route may change according to the weather and the judgment of the guides.
When to go

Nepal has two main trekking seasons: spring, before the monsoon, and fall, after it. The monsoon usually runs from June to September. In winter, from December to February, snow and severe cold on the pass raise the risk, and some teahouses on the upper part of the route may close.

Our expeditions depart in the two good windows, in April and May and in September and October. In spring there is a greater chance of meeting snow left on the pass from the winter, and in the fall the skies are usually clearer. You will find the current dates on the expedition page.
Permits, visa and insurance

To enter the area you need the Annapurna Conservation Area entry permit, ACAP. It costs 3,000 Nepalese rupees for a foreign visitor (as of 2026), and it is checked at several checkpoints along the route. The entry permits are included in the price of our trek.

Most visitors, including UK, EU, US, Canadian and Australian citizens, get a Nepal tourist visa on arrival at Kathmandu airport or apply online in advance. For a 16-day trip you need the 30-day visa, which costs 50 US dollars (as of 2026) and is not included. Travel and medical insurance is not included either. Before buying, check that the policy covers trekking up to 5,416 m, including helicopter rescue.
Annapurna or Everest Base Camp

The two best-known treks in Nepal are different from each other. The Everest Base Camp trek goes higher, up to Kala Patthar at 5,545 m, and centers on the altitude challenge and a close view of the highest mountain in the world, 8,848 m. With us it lasts 19 days and is graded hard. The Annapurna Circuit is more varied in scenery and culture, crosses one high pass, lasts 16 days with us and is graded moderate. We have written a full guide of its own to Everest Base Camp.

content.value: What it costs and what is included

The Annapurna Circuit trek costs 2,500 US dollars per person. It includes transfers between the airport and the hotel in Kathmandu, dinners at a restaurant before and after the trek, 3 nights in a 4-star hotel in Kathmandu in a single room with breakfast, a night in a 4-star hotel in Pokhara in a single room with breakfast, internal jeep transfers, a domestic flight from Pokhara to Kathmandu at the end of the trek, teahouse accommodation in shared rooms throughout the trek, all entry permits for the trek and the Annapurna Conservation Area, three meals a day from the menu, 2 liters of hot water a day, a shower and attached toilet where available on the route, professional local English-speaking guides, porters for personal gear up to 15 kg per person, a first aid kit carried by the guides, a pulse oximeter for the group and a satellite device, a personal area in the HighAir app, a personal gear checklist with an online gear consultation, an online preparation call with your group and guide, and a gift kit with a cap, a dry-fit shirt and a 100-liter duffel bag.

Not included: international flights, travel and medical insurance, lunch and dinner at the hotels in Kathmandu and Pokhara, personal gear, tips for guides and porters (250 dollars per person), the Nepal visa (50 dollars), vaccinations and travel clinic advice, and the extras the teahouses charge for separately, such as internet, laundry, alcohol and additional meals. A fourth hotel night in Kathmandu, if needed, is not included. A single room in the teahouses costs 20 dollars a night.
Keep in mind that in the event of an early descent from the mountain, for any reason, the additional costs, such as extra nights, meals and flight changes, are the traveler's responsibility.
The Annapurna Circuit with HighAir
At HighAir we take groups on the Annapurna Circuit in spring and fall. Our trek lasts 16 days, the group is limited to 10 participants, and the success rate we publish for this trek is 90 percent.
Anyone who comes back from the Thorong La wanting more can think about the next step: a first summit above 6,000 m, such as Mera Peak or Island Peak in the Everest region.

A portion of the proceeds from every expedition we run is dedicated to supporting cancer patients, because the mountains, in our view, are also a way of giving back. Every climber you see on the summits of the world started once, on one mountain or on one trail. If the Annapurna Circuit is your trail, we are here.
Frequently asked questions
How many days does the Annapurna Circuit trek take?

HighAir's trek, which also includes Tilicho Lake, lasts 16 days from arrival in Kathmandu to departure. Nine of them are on the trail, from Chame to Muktinath, including an acclimatization day in Manang. The road sections at the start and end of the trek are covered by jeep, and from Pokhara you fly back to Kathmandu.
What is the highest point on the Annapurna Circuit?

The highest point is the Thorong La pass, 5,416 m, one of the highest mountain passes in the world crossed on foot. The highest overnight stop is Thorong High Camp, 4,880 m, and on our route you also climb to Tilicho Lake, 4,919 m.
How hard is the Annapurna Circuit, and do I need experience?

We grade the trek as moderate, and no climbing experience is required. The difficulty is the altitude, the long days and the pass day, when you set out in the dark and descend more than 1,600 m. Anyone who can walk about 20 km a day and comes with strong motivation can be suited to the trek, and a medical certificate is required from every participant.
When is the best season for the Annapurna Circuit?
Spring and fall, before and after the monsoon. Our expeditions depart in April and May and in September and October. In winter, snow and severe cold on the pass raise the risk.
Which permits do you need for the Annapurna Circuit?

You need the Annapurna Conservation Area entry permit, ACAP, which costs 3,000 Nepalese rupees for a foreign visitor (as of 2026). It is included in the price of our trek, while the Nepal visa, 50 dollars for 30 days, is not.
What language do the guides speak?
The trek is led by professional local guides from Nepal who speak English and have long experience leading groups in the mountains.
